title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
abstract: We study the global $V$-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential $u$ (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time $V$-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.
summary: This paper rigorously examines the global V-representability of TDDFT for the Hubbard dimer model, a minimal model for correlated electrons. It proves that the non-interacting dynamics can be successfully continued across 'singular times' where standard theoretical tools fail. This advances the theoretical understanding of how TDDFT describes complex quantum dynamics in strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the global V-representability problem in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) for the Hubbard dimer model, specifically focusing on dynamics beyond singular times.
main_result: The authors prove global-in-time V-representability for both conventional and geometric formulations of TDDFT, showing that singular times do not obstruct the continuation of non-interacting dynamics.
method: The analysis involves comparing the time evolution derived from the interacting Hubbard Hamiltonian with the dynamics predicted by non-interacting Kohn-Sham equations, utilizing both variational and geometric formulations of TDDFT.
model_or_system: The system is the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. The dynamics are governed by a time-dependent Hamiltonian, and the analysis is restricted to the low-dimensional subspace representing the two-particle spin-singlet Slater states.
key_observables: The time-dependent density ($ho(t, \mathbf{x})$) and the effective potentials ($v$ or $w$) are key observables used to test representability.
important_parameters: The hopping parameter ($	au$), on-site interaction parameters ($U_1, U_2$), and the external potential $u(t)$ are crucial parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis builds upon the framework of TDDFT, addressing the breakdown of standard inversion formulas at singular times, and requires the non-interacting trajectories to belong to $W^{1,1}(0, T; \mathbb{C}^3)$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing VP-representable densities, then analyzing non-interacting trajectories for the Variational Principle (VP), followed by a similar characterization for the Geometric Principle (GP), culminating in the main theorem proving global-in-time continuation.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the fundamental theoretical limitations of TDDFT, particularly concerning the continuation of dynamics across singularities, which is a major hurdle in simulating strongly correlated materials.
